title: A linked list of ints
description:
Write a singly linked list from scratch, with a private nested `Node` class and `head` and `tail` references (no `java.util` collections inside):

```java
class IntLinkedList {
    void addFirst(int value)
    void addLast(int value)
    int removeFirst()                 // NoSuchElementException when empty
    int get(int index)                // IndexOutOfBoundsException outside 0..size-1
    int indexOf(int value)            // first index, or -1
    int removeAll(int value)          // removes every node holding value; returns how many
    void reverse()                    // in place, O(n), no new nodes
    int middle()                      // the middle value, the second of the two middles for an even size; one pass
    int size()
    String toString()                 // "[1, 2, 3]"
}
```

`middle` must walk the list once, using two references that move at different speeds; `removeAll` must also keep `tail` correct, so that `addLast` still works afterwards.
hints: Draw boxes and arrows for the empty list, a one-node list, and changes at the head and tail; most bugs are in those cases.
For `middle`, move one reference one step and another two steps at a time: when the fast one reaches the end, the slow one is in the middle.
rules: Build the list from your own nodes, without java.util collections.
